significance: Built in 1049 by Emperor Ly Thai Tong and refined in 1105 under Ly Nhan Tong, this small hexagonal shrine to Avalokiteshvara stands on a single stone pillar 1.25 metres across and 4 metres high, shaped so that the whole rises like a lotus, the Buddhist emblem of purity. Destroyed in 1954, it was rebuilt the following year by North Vietnam's Ministry of Culture; a replica was raised near Saigon in the late 1950s.
story: The emperor is said to have dreamed of Avalokiteshvara seated on a lotus handing him a son; a son was born after he married a peasant girl, and he built the lotus-shaped shrine in thanks.
